headline: House Republicans picked Jim Jordan.
summary: Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio beat Steve Scalise 106-73 Tuesday in a secret ballot to lead House Republicans in the minority. Jordan, 62, co-founded the Freedom Caucus and chairs the Judiciary Committee. He told colleagues 'offense, not defense, wins elections.' Trump stayed out of it. Democrats pick their leaders next week.

cover_question.q: Why pick a leader if you lost?

cover_answer: The losing side still needs a captain. He picks the fights.
table_question: After a big loss, do you want a steady captain or a fighter?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The Republicans in Congress lost a big vote last week, so now they are the smaller team. On Tuesday they picked a new captain, a man named Jim Jordan from Ohio. It's like a soccer team that lost picking who leads the next game. Nothing changes at our house.
5-7.why: A team that lost and a new captain: the whole story at this age. The Freedom Caucus stays out.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script gives them a team that lost picking a new captain, which they have seen on a field. The Freedom Caucus never comes up. Expect 'is he the boss now?' No. The president is still the president, and the other party runs the House.

8-12.script: Republicans lost the House last week, and their old leader is stepping aside. On Tuesday they picked a new one by secret ballot, folded papers nobody can trace, like a class president vote. Jim Jordan beat Steve Scalise 106-73. Scalise had been No. 2 for 12 years, and most wanted a change.
8-12.why: A secret ballot and a count: a rule to check, a result to argue with.
8-12.why_long: At eight they are working out rules and whether adults apply them, so the script hands over the secret ballot, a vote by folded paper, and a count they can check: 106 to 73. The class president vote is the mechanism they know. Expect 'why secret?' So nobody gets punished for their pick. Scalise keeps his seat.

13-17.script: Does the losing side's leader matter? Democrats can pass big votes now without Republican help. Still, 106 of them chose Jim Jordan over Steve Scalise, a fighter over a 12-year insider. Jordan says 'offense, not defense, wins elections.' Second: is picking the loudest fighter how a party learns from a loss?
13-17.why: Powerless and newly led, both true. Is a fighter a plan? Let them say.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: Republicans cannot stop a House vote now, and they still chose who speaks for them. The script asks whether a fighter is a plan, and at 13 they are testing whether you will argue it honestly. Expect 'what does he want to do?' The articles do not say. Tell them so.

5-7.a: The boss of the smaller team in Congress. They lost the election, so they have fewer seats, and one person speaks for all of them.

8-12.q: Why pick a leader if you lost?
8-12.a: Every team has a captain, win or lose. His job is the plan to win it back.

8-12.q: Why him and not the other guy?
8-12.a: Scalise had been No. 2 since 2014. Most wanted a change after losing.

13-17.q: Is 'offense, not defense' a plan or a slogan?
13-17.a: He cites committee fights. The articles name no policy. You decide.

13-17.q: Does the losing side's leader even matter?
13-17.a: Semafor says Democrats can pass key votes without him. His job is 2028.

caption:
The losing side still needs a captain. He picks the fights.

Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio beat Steve Scalise 106-73 Tuesday in a secret ballot to lead House Republicans in the minority. Jordan, 62, co-founded the Freedom Caucus and chairs the Judiciary Committee. He told colleagues 'offense, not defense, wins elections.' Trump stayed out of it. Democrats pick their leaders next week.
